newsitem.title: USA: Mandela talks of his success - report.
newsitem.headline: Mandela talks of his success - report.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said the success he has achieved in remaking his country is "beyond our wildest expectations," the New York Times reported in its Sunday edition.
"What can be more dramatic than that?" the 78-year-old Mandela told the Times in an hour-long interview conducted with the newspaper in his home in Johannesburg.
Among the successes Mandela mentioned was the 3.5 percent economic growth rate achieved in the last year.
He also boasted about the "700 water supply projects are under way, which will give 6.4 million people access to water ... where people have never had clean tap water."
"On health ... over 5.5 million schoolchildren in poor area are benefiting from the primary school nutrition programme," he said.

Mandela admitted to difficulty in remaking the country's police force which he said is plagued with corrupt officers who have little experience in fighting crime and apparently no understanding of individual rights.
"There are rogue elements, some of them in key positions," Mandela said.

The Times said Mandela turned aside several questions including whether Deputy President Thabo Mbeki will succeed him and whether he believed former President F. W. de Klerk had directly ordered atrocities against blacks.
"I'd like to avoid that if you don't mind," Mandela said.

He also denied recent speculation that he would step down before the end of 1999 but said he would give up his post as party president next year to open the field to young people "who are really more energetic, more assertive and who are deep thinkers with better vision."
